relevance_note: Case report of a girl with HA20: "Both WES and CNV analyses indicated that the patient had lost the paternal allele of the TNFAIP3 gene, leading to HA20."
method_note: I read the paper, the schema (schema_ha20_v5.json) and extraction_rules_v1.md only; no other file was opened, no script transcribed any table, and no value comes from memory. Scope: the proband (label 'patient', rule 5), her tested parents (the paper's own labels II-2 and II-1, rule 1), and the four previously published HA20 patients shown as columns of Table 1 (v4 label rule 'Table <n> column <k>', k counting data columns from the left; Table 1 column 1 is the present patient, so the literature patients are columns 2-5). The grandparents are mentioned only collectively ('DNA was extracted from the peripheral blood leukocytes of the patient, her parents, and her grandparents'; Fig. 1D pedigree, which I cannot read); the paper gives no individual-level fact, no label and no count for them, so I created no rows and note this as an uncertainty. Table 1 spans: for the short rows (Gender, Initial symptoms, Symptom onset, Age at diagnosis, Treatment, References) I quote the row from its label through that patient's cell; for the very long Phenotype and Involved genes rows I quote only the cell, because the full row segment exceeds 300 characters. The paper prints the same variant both as 'c.305A > G' (main text) and as 'NM_001270507.2(TNFAIP3):c.305A>G' (Fig. 1 legend); I used the figure-legend form as the value and its string as the span. Uncertainties and judgement calls, all recorded deliberately: (1) variant_type for all five deletions is 'large deletion/CNV' - the schema's only deletion class - although the paper's own words are 'microdeletion'/'deletion' and one is only 5 kb; (2) 'gene_symbol_as_stated' = 'TNFAIP3' for Table 1 columns 3-5, where the 'Involved genes' cell prints 'TNFAIP3, PERP' (columns 3-4) or a list of about 50 genes including TNFAIP3 (column 5); (3) I did not create a variant row for the father (II-1): the paper prints only that he 'was homozygous for the reference allele (G/G)'; (4) I created a c.305A>G row for the patient and her mother because the paper calls it 'This variant' and reports each person's genotype; the authors also note it 'is relatively common (MAF = 0.0117) in the Japanese population' and it is the deletion, not this SNP, that they say led to HA20; (5) the patient's zygosity for the deletion is 'heterozygous' from the conclusion sentence about the present case and from the loss of one (paternal) allele, and the c.305A>G inheritance is 'inherited maternal' because the paper states her mother carries that variant; (6) the paper states 'Although she was afebrile' at the 8-month examination while also reporting intermittent fevers from age 3 weeks and 'Periodic fever' in Table 1 - I read the afebrile statement as a single-time-point finding, so I emitted an 'excluded' row for 'fever' and kept the checklist item 'recurrent fever' as observed, rather than treating it as a contradiction; (7) 'clinical_diagnosis_basis' is genetic testing (WES, CNV analysis, SNP array) - the paper also records that her symptoms did not fulfil the criteria for complete or incomplete Behcet disease; (8) for whole-panel normals and infection screens (immunological workup 'no apparent abnormalities', T-SPOT, EBV-IgM/IgG, C7-HRP, stool culture 'negative for enteric infection', HLA-B51 negative) I emitted no rows, following D-27 (they name no specific abnormality) - noted here; (9) the supplement table's first column is blank, so its rows carry no patient label and I quoted single cells; (10) hpo_id_candidate is null everywhere: I had no ontology file to verify IDs against and rule 2 forbids guessing. (11) Internal discrepancy in the paper: the same deletion is printed as '187 kb' (WES/EXCAVATOR2 sentence) and as '119 kb' (SNP array sentence, abstract, Table 1); I recorded the 119 kb description because it is the one the paper prints with coordinates and repeats in Table 1, and note the 187 kb figure here rather than creating a second variant row. (12) 'n_patients_reported' = 5 counts the patients with a TNFAIP3 deletion this document describes or tabulates (the present patient plus the four Table 1 columns), matching 'five of 69 (7.2%) patients diagnosed with HA20 carried a deletion predicted to result in HA20'. (13) 'cohort_size_as_stated' is null: the only study-level count the paper gives, 69, is the total of HA20 patients in its literature survey (reference 3 and refs 8-16), not the number of patients of this study, so I did not record it there; the survey patients other than the four tabulated in Table 1 get no rows and are counted nowhere. Table symbols: Table 1 has a single '-' style cell, the '—' in the 'Range of deletion' row of column 2, which I treat as not reported for that patient's genomic coordinates (no legend defines it). (v6, D-31) I checked the whole paper for the stacked-cell separator ' / ' and found none, so no cell had to be treated as stacked; the only slashes are inside words ('oral/perianal ulcers', 'autoinflammatory and/or autoimmune') and the 'Involved genes' cells of Table 1 columns 3-5 are comma-separated gene lists, not stacked per-patient values. Two further notes on Table 1: the same reference '(Tsuchida et al.^8)' appears in two adjacent columns, and I kept those as two separate people, as the table presents them; and Table 1 column 1 is the present patient ('This report'), so the four literature patients are columns 2-5.
